title: Microgeneration Certification Scheme: what it means and why it matters
subtitle: How MCS certification affects grant eligibility, SEG payments, and consumer protection
excerpt: The Microgeneration Certification Scheme (MCS) is the industry quality mark for small-scale renewable energy installations in the UK. Without an MCS-certified installation, a household cannot claim the Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant, receive Smart Export Guarantee payments, or make a valid claim under the installer's warranty if something goes wrong.
sourceNotes: MCS standards documents MCS 001 (solar PV), MCS 006 (solar thermal), MCS 007 (heat pumps), all available free at mcscertified.com. BEIS Boiler Upgrade Scheme guidance: eligibility requirements. Ofgem Smart Export Guarantee rules: eligibility for licensed exporters.

glossaryTerms.definition: A quality mark for small-scale renewable energy installations and installers in the UK. MCS certification is a prerequisite for most government grants and Smart Export Guarantee payments.
A government-mandated scheme requiring larger electricity suppliers to offer export tariffs to eligible small-scale generators. Replaces the old Feed-in Tariff export payment.
A UK government grant scheme providing £7,500 toward the cost of installing a heat pump (2026 rate, England and Wales). The installation must be carried out by an MCS-certified installer.

content.text: MCS certification covers both the product and the installer. For a householder, the key check is that the installer is listed on the MCS register at mcscertified.com. A system installed by a non-MCS company does not qualify as an MCS installation, even if the products are MCS-certified.
grant (heat pumps). The installer applies on behalf of the householder and deducts the grant amount from the invoice.
payments for solar PV and other qualifying technologies. SEG tariff rates vary by supplier; each licensed supplier sets its own rate above zero.
An MCS installation certificate. This is required for some home insurance policies and for Property Information Forms during a property sale.
Recourse through the MCS Compliance Scheme if the installer does not honour the warranty or rectify defects.
Go to mcscertified.com and search by installer name and postcode. Confirm the certificate is current (not lapsed) and covers the relevant technology (MCS 001 for solar PV; MCS 007 for heat pumps).
Ask the installer for their MCS certificate number before signing a contract. Legitimate installers give this without hesitation.
After installation, the installer registers the system with MCS and provides a certificate of compliance. Keep this with your property documents.

rows.symptom: Installer claims to be MCS-certified but is not on the register
rows.cause: Their certification may have lapsed, or they are trading under a different company name on the register
rows.fix: Do not proceed until the certificate is verified on the MCS website. Ask for the exact MCS certificate number and check it directly. Do not accept a photocopy of a certificate as proof of current certification.
